intro.title: A dictionary maps keys to values
intro.body: Square brackets read and write a key. .get(key, default) avoids a KeyError when the key is missing, which makes dictionaries perfect for counting.

challenges.explanation: The value 3 is incremented by 2 and stored back under the same key.

challenges.prompt: Read the score for "ada" without crashing if the key is missing.
challenges.explanation: dict.get(key, default) returns the default instead of raising KeyError.

challenges.statement: Two entries in a dictionary can share the same key.
challenges.explanation: Keys are unique; assigning an existing key replaces its value.

challenges.prompt: This crashes when the word is new. Tap the line and pick the fix.
challenges.explanation: counts[word] does not exist yet on the first sighting, so get(word, 0) supplies a starting count.

challenges.prompt: Read a word and print how many different letters it contains.

starterCode.python:
word = input().strip()
# print the number of distinct letters

challenges.explanation: Set or dictionary keys both collapse duplicates; len(set(word)) is the shortest answer.
